S17.01.needs: an account or local runtime that can answer
S17.01.note: The author label is a visually hidden line that prefixes the answer as 'AGI (<model>) replied:' in the code; the visible difference is by layout and the model name shown in the meta line.
steps: Open the AGI Code view from the activity bar and type a short question in the composer.
Press Send and wait for the answer to finish.
Look for the model name shown with the answer (hover the answer's small meta line for the token detail).
Turn on VoiceOver and move to the answer: it should announce the answer as from AGI with the model name, not as your message.
Compare with Expected: the answer must look and sound different from your own message, and name the model.
S17.01.where: AGI Code sidebar (activity bar icon "AGI Code") > type a question and press Send > look at the answer

S17.02.needs: an account or local runtime that can answer
S17.02.note: The 'Stop response' control is icon-only with a tooltip, so it is a useful marker to find while the answer streams.
steps: Ask for a longer answer that uses a list, bold text and a code block, for example 'Explain a sorting algorithm with a code example'.
Watch the answer while it arrives, without clicking anything.
Check that text appears a little at a time, not all at once at the end.
Check that the list, bold words and code block are formatted as they arrive.
Compare with Expected: the answer must fill in gradually with formatting shown on the way.
S17.02.where: AGI Code sidebar > type a question and press Send > watch the answer area while it is still arriving

S17.03.needs: an account or local runtime that can answer
S17.03.note: The indicator is an image mark with an aria-label, and the 'Starting…' text only appears with the Activity row.
steps: Send a question that takes a few seconds to answer.
Look straight after you press Send, before any text appears, for the small AGI mark that appears as the answer's placeholder.
Turn on VoiceOver and move to that mark: it should be announced as 'AGI is responding'.
Look for the 'Activity' row with 'Starting…' if the answer uses tools.
Compare with Expected: a working indicator must show before and during the answer, and be announced.
S17.03.where: AGI Code sidebar > type a question and press Send > watch the space under your message before the text arrives

S17.04.needs: an account or local runtime that can answer, and a workspace folder
S17.04.note: Only a collapsible Activity (tool steps) summary was found; no separate reasoning-summary disclosure was found in the webview code.
steps: Ask a question that needs AGI to read a file or run a tool.
When the answer shows an 'Activity' row above it, click that row.
Check that the row opens and closes, showing its steps and a chevron.
Press Tab to the row and press Return or Space to open and close it with the keyboard.
Compare with Expected: the summary of work must collapse and expand on demand. The model's reasoning text itself was not found in this screen.
S17.04.where: AGI Code sidebar > send a message that makes AGI use a tool (for example 'Read the README in this workspace') > click the 'Activity' row above the answer

S17.05.needs: an account or local runtime that can answer, and a workspace folder
steps: Ask for something that uses a tool, such as 'List the files in this folder'.
Wait for the 'Activity' row to appear above the answer and click it open.
Click one of the tool steps to expand it.
Check that each step shows the tool's name, a status (running, done or error) and its result.
Compare with Expected: each tool call must show its name, status and result.
S17.05.where: AGI Code sidebar > send a message that makes AGI use a tool > click the 'Activity' row > expand one tool step

S17.15.needs: an account or local runtime that can answer
S17.15.note: The copy takes the answer's stored source text (the text the code keeps for the answer), not a separately rendered plain-text version; the tester should judge the pasted result against Expected.
steps: Send a question and wait for the answer to finish.
Move the pointer over the answer to show its action icons.
Click the copy icon, the first one, whose tooltip is 'Copy'.
Paste into a text editor (Cmd+V) to see the copied text.
Compare with Expected: the whole answer's text must be on the clipboard, and the icon should briefly show 'Copied'.
S17.15.where: AGI Code sidebar > send a message > hover the answer > click the copy icon (tooltip 'Copy')

S17.19.needs: an account or local runtime that can answer
S17.19.note: The button is shown only on the latest answer (CSS class message--latest).
steps: Send a question and wait until the answer is complete.
Hover over the latest answer and find the refresh icon, tooltip 'Regenerate'.
Click it.
Check that a new answer replaces the previous attempt for the same question in the same place.
Compare with Expected: a new attempt for the same prompt must appear, not a copy of the old one.
S17.19.where: AGI Code sidebar > send a message > wait for the answer to finish > hover the latest answer > click the refresh icon (tooltip 'Regenerate')

S17.20.needs: a way to make the next answer fail (for example, turn off the internet)
S17.20.note: The Retry button appears only when the failure is marked retryable; the code shows it as a button in the error block.
steps: Turn off the internet connection, or otherwise make the next answer fail.
Send a question and wait for the error block to appear.
Read the error block and find the 'Retry' button.
Turn the internet back on, then click 'Retry'.
Compare with Expected: the failure must be replaced by the new outcome; the error block should disappear and the new answer should appear.
S17.20.where: AGI Code sidebar > cause a failed answer (for example, turn off the internet and press Send) > click 'Retry' in the error block

S17.27.needs: an account or local runtime that can answer
S17.27.note: The new session's history and the unchanged original were not checked against code beyond the branch handler.
steps: Send two or more messages so there is an earlier answer.
Hover an earlier answer and click the fork icon, tooltip 'Branch from here'.
Check that a new session opens with the conversation up to that answer.
Go back to the original session and check it still has all its messages.
Compare with Expected: the new session keeps history up to that answer and the original is unchanged.
S17.27.where: AGI Code sidebar > send a message > hover an answer > click the fork icon 'Branch from here'

S17.29.needs: an account or local runtime that can answer
S17.29.note: The recorded feedback is sent to the server; the UI only shows the pressed state.
steps: Send a question and wait for the answer to finish.
Hover the answer and click the thumbs-up icon, tooltip 'Good response'.
Check that the icon fills in and reads as pressed.
Click it again and check the tooltip changes to 'Remove rating' and the icon clears.
Compare with Expected: a thumbs-up must record positive feedback for that answer; the UI shows only the pressed state, so the record itself cannot be seen here.
S17.29.where: AGI Code sidebar > send a message > hover the answer > click the thumbs-up icon 'Good response'

S17.30.needs: an account or local runtime that can answer
S17.30.note: The recorded feedback is sent to the server; the UI only shows the pressed state.
steps: Send a question and wait for the answer to finish.
Hover the answer and click the thumbs-down icon, tooltip 'Bad response'.
Check that the icon fills in and reads as pressed.
Click it again and check the tooltip changes to 'Remove rating' and the icon clears.
Compare with Expected: a thumbs-down must record negative feedback for that answer; the UI shows only the pressed state, so the record itself cannot be seen here.
S17.30.where: AGI Code sidebar > send a message > hover the answer > click the thumbs-down icon 'Bad response'

S17.36.needs: an account or local runtime that can answer
S17.36.note: No cost figure was found in the answer details; time is shown only per tool step in the Activity row.
steps: Send a question and wait for the answer to finish.
Look at the small text line under the answer; it shows the model that answered.
Hover that line to see the token details (input and output tokens).
If the answer used prompt caching, look for the 'Prompt cache' line below it.
Compare with Expected: the model that actually answered and its token usage must be visible. No cost figure was found in this area.
S17.36.where: AGI Code sidebar > send a message > look at the small line under the answer (the model name), then hover it

S17.37.needs: a way to cut the connection while an answer streams (for example, turn off the internet)
S17.37.note: The label is the English template with a {provider} placeholder that the app fills in; the code keeps partial text and marks it retryable, but no separate 'incomplete' wording was found.
steps: Send a long question that streams for a while.
Turn off the internet while the answer is still arriving.
Look at the partial text that already arrived; it should stay on screen.
Read the error block below it for the words about the stop and its reason.
Compare with Expected: the partial answer must stay and be marked incomplete, with the reason shown in the error block.
S17.37.where: AGI Code sidebar > send a message > the answer stops partway (for example, the connection drops while it streams) > read the error block below the partial answer

labels.text: The safety system stopped this response. Rephrase the request, or try a different model.

S17.38.needs: a request the safety system refuses
S17.38.note: The refusal has its own sentence, but it uses the same error block as other failures; no separate visual refusal state was found.
steps: Send a request that the safety system is likely to refuse.
Wait for the error block to appear under the turn.
Read the words in the error block.
Compare with Expected: it must say a safety refusal with a next step ('Rephrase the request, or try a different model.'), not a generic error.
S17.38.where: AGI Code sidebar > send a message that the safety system refuses > read the error block

S17.39.needs: an account or local runtime that can answer
S17.39.note: The stop path posts a done message with stopped set, but the webview's handling of that flag did not show which words appear; 'The turn was stopped.' is the words for an interrupted failure.
steps: Send a long question.
While the answer is still arriving, click the 'Stop response' button.
Check that the answer stops and keeps the text that already arrived.
Look for the 'Stopped' marker or the note about the stopped turn, and whether a Retry option is offered.
Compare with Expected: the answer must be marked stopped, keep what arrived, and offer to try again. The exact words shown after a user stop were not confirmed in the code.
S17.39.where: AGI Code sidebar > send a message > click the 'Stop response' button while the answer streams > read the note on the answer

S17.40.needs: a turn that returns no output (hard to trigger on demand)
S17.40.note: The CLI maps an empty response to a provider-unavailable failure, and the extension shows the words '{provider} could not answer.'; no separate 'no response' wording was found in the English strings, and whether Retry is offered depends on the protocol's retryable flag, which was not checked.
steps: Send a message that the model answers with nothing (this depends on the provider; it may be hard to trigger).
Wait for the error block under the turn.
Read the words: they should say the provider could not answer.
Check whether a 'Retry' button is offered.
Compare with Expected: an explicit error with retry must appear, not an empty bubble.
S17.40.where: AGI Code sidebar > send a message that gets no reply from the model > read the error block
